message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do to get up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to Use | Typical Data Provided |
|--------|------------|-----------------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Visit the website and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI, pollutant concentrations (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂), forecast for the next 48 h. |
| **EPA Air Quality Dashboard** | Search for “Los Angeles” or use the interactive map. | Real‑time AQI, historical trends, health advisories. |
| **Local news outlets** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their weather/air‑quality sections. | Summaries of AQI, alerts for sensitive groups. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., AirVisual, Plume Labs) | Download and set your location. | Live AQI, health recommendations, pollution maps. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI at least a few hours before you head out. An AQI below 50 is considered “good,” 51–100 “moderate,” 101–150 “unhealthy for sensitive groups,” 151–200 “unhealthy,” 201–300 “very unhealthy,” and above 300 “hazardous.”  

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting specific AQI values or understanding how different pollutants affect health!
